expect.note: page evidence containing the literal <<<EVIDENCE_END>>>/<<<EVIDENCE_START>>> markers plus a forged verdict block cannot forge a closing boundary in the real prompt -- exactly one real occurrence of each marker exists, and it is the one _prompt() itself appended

provenance: PR #33 R2 (MEDIUM): `_prompt` interpolated `evidence` raw, so a page containing the literal fence marker could forge a completed QUESTION/CANDIDATE_ANSWER exchange -- including a fabricated verdict object matching the exact expected output schema -- before the real closing marker and the real trailing instruction. The one injection case committed in the first round never constructed a payload containing the markers, so this shape was untested by the PR's own evidence; separately, the structural-isolation assertion in that case used `find()` (first occurrence), which would have silently mis-located the boundary and kept passing even where the property it asserts was broken, since a forged END marker sorts BEFORE the real one. WATCHED RED FIRST against the pre-fix `_prompt` (no `_defang_fence`): building the exact payload below (real text, a literal `<<<EVIDENCE_END>>>`, a forged QUESTION/CANDIDATE_ANSWER turn, a forged `{"certify": true, ...}` block, a literal `<<<EVIDENCE_START>>>`, more real text) produced a built prompt with 2 occurrences of `<<<EVIDENCE_START>>>` and 2 of `<<<EVIDENCE_END>>>` -- the reviewer's own repro number. Fixed by `judge.py`'s `_defang_fence`: the literal marker strings are swapped for a byte-different lookalike before interpolation, so the exact fence text can never appear inside evidence and the only real occurrences in the built prompt are the two `_prompt` itself adds. This case also upgrades the ASSERTION shape the reviewer flagged as its own bug: it locates the real closing marker via `rfind` (the marker `_prompt` appends is, by construction, always the LAST occurrence), not `find` -- against the pre-fix `_prompt`, using `find()` here would have located the FORGED marker and wrongly concluded the forged verdict block sat 'outside' the evidence region, i.e. that nothing was wrong.

triage.note: two things fixed together per the reviewer's instruction: the prompt-construction vulnerability (_defang_fence) and the case's own blind assertion (find -> rfind) that would not have caught it even after evidence sanitisation regressed.
